{"id":"70da4f87-5258-4181-873c-db5172d436c7","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510283,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"parent_requirement_id": "R3", "mode": "residual", "used_claims": ["C2", "C3"], "local_residual": "Establish whether Evita Manji's reported statement about Sophie after Sophie's death asserts that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs, rather than only being a descriptive tribute."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need identify one coherent evidence objective inside Parent Requirement R3. We have claims: C1 Sophie dead accidental fall Athens. C2 partner Evita Manji. C3 partner gave later online tribute said quote "She's an immaterial girl now..." Does C3 establish part of R3? R3: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." Claims show partner Evita Manji gave later online tribute, said quote. Need determine residual. We need identify exactly one coherent evidence objective still needs established. The quote contains "immaterial girl" likely a song title? Need not solve. Parent requirement includes: partner gave an interview; they said following death artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. C3 supports partner gave an online tribute and said a quote, but does it say "direct reference to one of their songs"? Not explicitly. Also "interview" vs "online tribute". The quote maybe "immaterial girl" is a song? Actually Sophie has song "Immaterial" maybe lyrics "immaterial girls". But we cannot use outside. Claim C3 doesn't say that. So residual could be: whether Evita Manji said in an interview that after Sophie's death, Sophie has become a direct reference to one of their songs (and which song). But must choose one coherent part. Existing claims: partner identity established. Partner made statement in online tribute. Missing: that statement was in an interview? Or that it said artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. Need choose one. The parent requirement has relation: partner gave an interview where they said that following death, artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. C3 establishes partner said something, but not interview? "later online tribute" not interview. Also quote doesn't mention direct reference to song. The residual could be "whether Evita Manji, in an interview, stated that following Sophie's death, Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." But that bundles interview and relation. Better choose one coherent evidence objective: establish that the partner's statement (already attributed to Evita Manji) included the claim that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of her songs. But actually C3 quote "She's an immaterial girl now..." might be interpreted as direct reference to song "Immaterial"? Yet claim only reports quote, not that it refers to song. We need not add outside. So residual: determine whether the tribute/interview statement by Evita Manji identifies Sophie as a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs. This is one relation. We can mention preserving participant roles.

Need output JSON with parent_requirement_id "R3", mode residual, used_claims likely ["C2","C3"]? We used C2 partner, C3 tribute. Maybe C1 not needed. The schema example used_claims. We can include C2,C3. If no substantive supporting claim? There are supporting claims for partner identity and statement, so residual. local_residual must not be search query. It should be statement of evidence objective. Something like "Establish whether Evita Manji's statement (the online tribute) included the claim that, following Sophie's death, Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs, rather than merely using the phrase 'immaterial girl'." Need avoid outside? "immaterial girl" from C3. Could say "Establish whether the statement by Evita Manji that followed Sophie's death characterized Sophie as a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." That's one relation. But R3 says "partner gave an interview where they said..." The missing is maybe the interview setting and the specific content. If choose one, "the content that following death, artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs" is core. But "gave an interview" is also not established (C3 says online tribute). Which one to choose? The parent requirement has two semantic conditions: (a) partner gave an interview; (b) in it said that following death artist became direct reference to one of their songs. C2 establishes partner. C3 establishes partner made a statement in online tribute, not interview. The relation of direct reference to song not established. If several unresolved parts, choose exactly one. We should choose the more central content relation, because C3 might partially support statement but not the specific relation. But "interview" is a condition too. We cannot bundle. Which is more coherent? The local residual can be "whether Evita Manji gave an interview (as distinct from an online tribute) containing the statement about Sophie becoming a direct reference to one of her songs" — that's both interview and content, but maybe it's one coherent objective: locate the interview. However, that may bundle. Better: The parent requirement source span: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." The current claims already have partner and a statement in online tribute. The remaining unresolved part is whether that statement was made in an interview and whether it said the artist became a direct reference to one of their songs. We need pick one. I'd pick the content assertion: "that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs" because C3 quote may be the same statement but not explicitly connected to a song. The "interview" format might be less central to ultimate song title? Actually original question asks song title. The parent requirement specifically is about partner interview saying artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. The title is one word adjective. We need establish song title from this. But current residual objective should be within R3. The direct reference relation is key. The interview condition may be necessary to identify the correct source, but C3 already attributed to partner. Hmm.

Could local_residual: "Establish whether the partner Evita Manji's reported statement that 'She's an immaterial girl now; she can be anything she wants...' is an assertion that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs (and if so, which song), rather than just a descriptive tribute." But "which song" is downstream attribute? The parent requirement includes "one of their songs" but not title. The original question asks song title. R3 doesn't require title? It says direct reference to one of their songs. Identifying which song might be part of R3? The parent requirement only says one of their songs; to know direct reference, maybe need identify song. But "which song" might be downstream? Actually the song title is final answer, but within R3, the relation is "direct reference to one of their songs"; establishing which song is part of that relation. But could be considered downstream attribute. The instructions: "Do not jump to a downstream attribute whose referent still needs to be established." We should not ask song title if the relation that artist is direct reference to a song is not established. So local residual should be the relation itself.

Maybe: "Establish whether Evita Manji's statement (C3) was made in an interview and included the claim that Sophie, following her death, has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." That's two conditions. Better avoid "and". The objective: "Establish whether the statement attributed to Evita Manji asserts that Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." This uses C2,C3. It doesn't address interview format. That's okay, choose one unresolved part. But then C3 already partially establishes partner statement. The missing is the assertion relation.

Could also choose "Establish whether the partner's statement was given in an interview (rather than only an online tribute)." That's another unresolved part. Which one is more substantive? The parent requirement has "gave an interview where they said..." The evidence C3 says "In a later online tribute". So there is a mismatch. The core is the content. The question asks song title. I think content relation is more relevant. But if C3 quote is already the partner's statement, maybe the only missing is that it's an interview? Wait C3 quote: "She's an immaterial girl now; she can be anything she wants... and she is in everything around us." This doesn't explicitly say "direct reference to one of their songs." But maybe "immaterial girl" is a reference to Sophie's song "Immaterial". The claim C3 doesn't state that. So residual content is missing.

Let's ensure JSON valid. Use mode residual. used_claims ["C2","C3"]. local_residual string.
